> **How to use this notebook**

> that escalate in difficulty:
>
> | Level               | What to do                                            |
> |----------------------------|--------------------------------------------|

> | **L2 — Fill-in**    | Replace `___` with correct code.                      |
> | **L3 — Free style** | Write all code yourself from the goal description.    |
> | **L4 — Scenario 1** | Real-world setting. Write full analysis.              |
> | **L5 — Scenario 2** | Complex multi-step scenario + short report.           |
>
> Needs the lmtest and car packages (`install.packages(c("lmtest", "car"))` once). Data: `cars`, `airquality` (built into R) and a small simulated data set.
>
> 📖 Matching lessons: https://t-daichiy.github.io/SQL_660/r650/m4_predict.html (650 M4 prediction & assumptions)

# Topic A — Predicting with a Regression Line


## Q1 · L1 · Reference

**Goal:** Predict stopping distance from speed (`cars`).

```{r q1-l1, eval=TRUE}
# === Complete example — read and run ===
fit <- lm(dist ~ speed, data = cars)
b <- coef(fit)
b
pred_hand <- b[1] + b[2] * 21              # speed = 21 mph
pred_r <- predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(speed = 21))
round(c(hand = unname(pred_hand), predict = unname(pred_r)), 3)
```

# Topic B — Confidence & Prediction Intervals


## Q6 · L1 · Reference

**Goal:** Compare the 95% CI for the mean distance and the 95% PI for one car at speed = 21.

```{r q6-l1, eval=TRUE}
# === Complete example — read and run ===
nd <- data.frame(speed = 21)
ci <- predict(fit, nd, interval = "confidence")
pi <- predict(fit, nd, interval = "prediction")
round(rbind(confidence = ci, prediction = pi), 2)
```

# Topic C — Checking the Assumptions


## Q11 · L1 · Reference

**Goal:** Look at the four standard diagnostic plots of the cars model.

```{r q11-l1, eval=TRUE}
# === Complete example — read and run ===
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(fit)              # residuals vs fitted, Q-Q, scale-location, leverage
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
round(summary(fit)$sigma, 3)
```

**Goal:** Check the normality of the residuals with a Q-Q plot and shapiro.test().

```{r q12-l2}
r <- ___(fit)
qqnorm(r); qqline(r, col = "red")
sw <- ___(r)
round(sw$p.value, 4)
```

# Topic D — Fixing Problems: Transformations & Robust SEs


## Q16 · L1 · Reference

**Goal:** Model log(Ozone) instead of Ozone and compare the residual normality.

```{r q16-l1, eval=TRUE}
# === Complete example — read and run ===
aq <- na.omit(airquality)
fit_raw <- lm(Ozone ~ Temp, data = aq)
fit_lg  <- lm(log(Ozone) ~ Temp, data = aq)
round(c(raw = shapiro.test(resid(fit_raw))$p.value, log = shapiro.test(resid(fit_lg))$p.value), 4)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2)); qqnorm(resid(fit_raw)); qqnorm(resid(fit_lg)); par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
